title: Rain
subtitle: We might just get what we wished for beneath its veil.

trails.title: Witness Report
trails.description: An unremarkable witness report. All rumors, whispers, and tales—every passerby keeps a few in their pockets.

content.text: A report from a special investigator mentions that her sound measurement equipment picked up steady infrasound at the Champ de Mars. The frequency and rhythm matched the calls of a whale—something impossible to hear in Paris. She tried to track the source but couldn't find it.

items.text: Without hesitation, Adèle rushes to Célia, trying to steady her friend.
Célia weakly shakes her head, stopping her.
The diviner looks past everyone, toward the darkening sky.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Just as it was meant to be.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: This ridiculous sight ... This distorted "Paris" ...
She smiles too, then lowers her gaze to the world below the tower.
The beasts below have donned new costumes, masquerading as humans. The strike becomes like a carnival parade.
More figures pour out from the alleys and buildings, half-beast, half-human, joining the wild hunt.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: The July Column just turned into a bilboquet, the Vert-Galant statue replaced with some bizarre lobster, and my friend is disappearing before my eyes.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: And you're telling me that all this was meant to happen?!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: It's all so-so meaningless, hah, so absurd.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Is it?
A single word pulls Beryl from her trance.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Hm. Perhaps you are right, Adèle. Thank you for showing me what I could not see.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Fate, destiny—it has become nothing more than an absurdity. A tangled mess.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: This "Storm" should never have come to pass.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: "Storm"?
She repeats the word faintly, glancing around.
Célia, too weak to speak; Félicienne, still unconscious; and Beryl—watching them both in silence.
Everyone is spent. Only one delirious actor remains on the stage.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: This "Storm" is quite the delightful surprise!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Look at this mass hysteria. It's becoming ever more unified!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: As if some force—some will—is drawing them together, controlling them.
He stumbles, penning the last stroke in his notebook.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Yes! Yes, I see it clearly now! The world is a stage—a performance with no script—and we have arrived at the moment when the curtain must fall and the scene must shift!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: This upheaval—this shift we've ushered in—has been intensifying the turmoil of the era!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: What a marvelous device! It's just the spark we need to ignite a cleansing fire.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: With this power, we can manipulate the appearance of the "Storm" as we please!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: The changes to the mass hysteria ... Yes, it's all obvious now. They were born from the collective subconscious. We are mere actors on this stage! For the material world is nothing but a projection of the mind!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Hahaha ... Hahahahahaha!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Their dialogues are but borrowed lines from ancient scripts! Their passion—their love for life—an oblivious repetition of the same narratives! The play has no script yet tells the same story! This material world—it is nothing more than a flicker on a cave wall!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: I've seen it—the ultimate truth! The truth that even the transcendental Law feigns to hide!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: But I've seen it now, hahahaha! I've seen it!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: The Depths of Myth itself will also be corrected, just as all the errors of the reality. But who decided which of these errors are "wrong" to begin with? Or perhaps, what is "right" is essentially an endlessly repeated chain of errors?! Hahaha ...!
Laurent Roseau bends backward, so sharply it seems as if he would snap in two. The reflected light of the sky-city shimmering in a reflection of his manic joy.
Beryl looks at him. Pity flickering across her tired face.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What's wrong with him?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: He has seen the fruition of his life's work, and it has driven him mad.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: But mad or not, none of it will matter soon.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: This whimsical era—along with the Paris we know—will be washed away in the coming rain.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Is this some kind of joke? Am I missing something?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: An era wiped out by a little rain? It doesn't make any sense.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No, Célia!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Paris—

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The city of light, of romance, and a tapestry of symbols.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Never shy in showing all manner of emotions—the chaotic passions of conflicting views, the conspiracies staged in her ancient alleys ...

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Because she defends your right to choose. To scream or fall silent. To look back or forward. To live under a monarchy or republic. And all manner of thought ...

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You may throw yourself into the maelstrom or conjure up a new one yourself.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Célia loves this city so deeply. She knows everything about Paris, from the catacombs to the top of every tower.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Célia deserves to live, not me!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Why? Why does Célia have to vanish?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: We stand in a vast garden surrounded by innumerable intersecting paths, welcoming endless forks, endless choices.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Hernani, Notre Dame, the hot air balloons drifting above the Palais Saint-Pierre ... Philosophies find their form, passing lip to lip and heart to heart through all her residents.
To regard fate and life with elegance and levity—that is the very spirit of Paris.
Where dreams and imaginings never fade—they stay with you across all times and eras, like a moveable feast.
Immortal. Indestructible.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No ...

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: What more is there for me to seek in this meaningless, inferior world? The "true" world—the one that matters—has already descended!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Voilà, see that? The clearest, most perfect water at the bottom of the Archive!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Now so close, almost within reach! In the deepest, most pristine layer of our joined consciousness!
Eternally real.
Eternally imprinted in the mind.
Eiffel Tower, Paris

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The rift is closing. The "Storm" will now correct the faults of this era.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The City of Light descending from the sky, the phantoms walking among the living, and the legendary beasts roaming the streets—they will all vanish.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The mad have fulfilled their wish. The play has come to an end. Everything once in chaos will be brought back to order.
No ...
Beryl ...
A hand clamps tight around Beryl's ankle.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Ah, you have awakened.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Though perhaps it would be better to remain asleep. It may spare you some pain.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: I ... I am no coward, Beryl!
She gasps, though no air, no wind, can fill what's left of her fading chest.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: But you have to fix this! You have to do something!

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Tell me how to change this, just a hint!

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: I refuse to vanish like this—to disappear after finally clawing my way back!
Beryl lifts her foot and steps forward without concern. Félicienne's fingers close desperately on empty air.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Those worthless grovelers who can't even use arcane skills! They deserve to die, not me!

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: This world belongs to us!

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Don't you dare turn your back on me, Beryl Bouanich!

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: I will report every moment of this to the Guiding One!
The retreating footsteps pause.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: I saw what you did to Laurent Roseau! You drove him to his death!

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: You've never been loyal to anyone! You're nothing but a soulless profiteer.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: You care for nothing! You never believed in any of the principles of Manus Vindictae! You never wanted to bring back the beautiful world we once had, did you?!
The sound of familiar steps approaches again, stopping right in front of her.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: How amusing.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You seek my help, yet accuse and threaten me in the same breath.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Do you think you speak to me from a position of strength? What would you do if our positions were reversed, dear Félicienne?
Beryl looks down at Félicienne as if examining a rare creature writhing in a deadly trap.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: There is nothing more to say.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: It has been a pleasure, madame.
Before Beryl can move, Félicienne trembles out a faint, broken sentence.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Hm?

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Ugh ...
She lowers her head, throat straining. Droplets slide from her hair and vanish into the dust.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Please ...

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Please help me ... Beryl ...

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: I ... I don't want to die ...!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Very well.
Beryl nods, straightens, and asks her final question.
But this time her translucent gaze settles on Adèle.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: What do you think, Adèle?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Should she be saved or pay for what she has done with her life?
